concepts.explanation: The 1947 to 1991 standoff between the US and Soviet Union, fought through proxies, spies and arms races, not direct war.
The Cold War divide between Soviet-controlled Eastern Europe and the West.
The secret US program that built the first atomic bombs during World War II.
The worldwide economic collapse of the 1930s, with mass unemployment and poverty.
The 1970s scandal where President Nixon's team spied on rivals and covered it up, forcing his resignation.
The 1950s US campaign of accusing people of communism with little evidence, ruining careers.
The 1962 standoff over Soviet missiles in Cuba, the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war.
The Nazi genocide of six million Jews and millions of others during World War II.
The Allied invasion of Nazi-occupied France on 6 June 1944, the largest seaborne invasion in history.
Japan's surprise attack on the US fleet in Hawaii in December 1941, bringing the US into World War II.
The barrier dividing East and West Berlin from 1961 to 1989. Its fall marked the Cold War's end.
The 14th to 17th century European revival of art, science and learning.
The 18th century movement putting reason and individual rights above tradition and authority.
The 18th and 19th century shift from hand production to machines and factories, reshaping society.
The 1920 to 1933 US ban on alcohol, which fuelled organised crime and secret bars.
Laws enforcing racial segregation in the US South from the late 1800s to the 1960s.
The 1950s and 60s struggle to end racial segregation and discrimination in the US.
Medieval wars launched by European Christians to seize the Holy Land from Muslim rule.
Catholic Church tribunals hunting heresy, notorious for torture and forced confessions.
South Africa's system of legalised racial segregation and white minority rule, 1948 to 1994.
The US and Soviet competition to dominate spaceflight, from Sputnik in 1957 to the Moon landing in 1969.
The 2001 al-Qaeda attacks on the US using hijacked planes, killing nearly 3,000 people.
US law passed after 9/11 expanding government surveillance and detention powers.
The Soviet Union's security and intelligence agency, feared for spying and repression.
East Germany's secret police, known for spying on its own citizens through informants.
Israel's national intelligence agency.
Britain's foreign intelligence service, home of the fictional James Bond.
The international police organisation coordinating cooperation between countries' police forces.
Organised crime families of Sicilian origin. A made man is a fully initiated member.
Japan's organised crime syndicates, known for strict hierarchy and full-body tattoos.
A criminal organisation controlling drug production and trafficking, mainly in Latin America.
An 18th century secret society, now a byword for conspiracy theories about hidden elites.
A centuries-old fraternal society with secret rituals, often the subject of conspiracy theories.
